summary: Three branches read from a local clone of TheTom/turboquant_plus. (1) experiment/temporal-decay@4ded8b8 is DOCS-ONLY: it adds docs/experiment-temporal-decay.md (38 lines), a design for progressive KV requantization turbo3->turbo2 (3.5->2.5 bit) for tokens older than ~70% of max_pos, triggered in llama_kv_cache::update(); age = seq_pos_max(seq_id) - cell.pos. Verdict in the doc: DESIGN COMPLETE, blocked on a turbo2 block type that does not exist; estimate 2-3 sessions. (2) experiment/temporal-decay-prototype@b42c027 is a misnomer: it contains NO temporal code, only M1 Max / M2 Pro community hardware diagnostics in scripts/README.md. The real prototype commit deb2d84 (2026-03-26, '3->2 requant VIABLE') is on main and test/villines-probe-validation. benchmarks/temporal_decay_prototype.py (426 lines) implements dequant turbo3 -> renormalize -> nearest 2-bit centroid -> recompute norm correction -> repack; 'zero-signs' remap is documented as broken/biased. Author-recorded numbers: synthetic d=128 turbo3 cos 0.983, decay 0.940 (>0.80); real Qwen3-1.7B 3-bit cos 0.985, decay 0.949 (>0.75; L0 0.971, L2 0.927); inner-product error 1.76x; estimated KV savings 30-34% at 32K-256K (256K: 1120->742 MB). (3) test/villines-probe-validation@846590d adds the Villines TV-divergence probe (tq_collapse_probe.py, 556 lines), k_channel_stats.py, torquant_certificate.py, tv_vs_ppl.py, a validation paper, and ~27k lines of result JSON. The probe monkey-patches scaled_dot_product_attention to capture real post-RoPE Q/K, quantizes K with the real turboquant package, and measures total-variation attention mass misrouted between FP16 and quantized distributions. It validates: K is load-bearing; Qwen-family K collapses at <=3-bit (turboMSE3 TV 0.370 on fp16 weights, matching PPL 3,556); the bias hypothesis is FALSIFIED (bias-free Qwen3-8B collapses 0.307, Mistral clean 0.091); the general mechanism is per-channel K off-centering (offset_ratio max: Qwen2.5 58.0, Qwen3 6.5, Mistral 2.5); per-head centering rescues 3.7x / 2.1x / none. Villines CUDA reference numbers reproduce within +/-0.010 on Metal. No tv_vs_ppl output JSON is committed, so the 'ghost PPL' TV->needle-NLL link is asserted, not measured. For the RTX 2070S 8GB box: keep K at q8_0 (asymmetric recipe) for Qwen3.5; centering is a partial low-bit rescue; temporal decay is a KV-memory lever that is designed but not implemented.

failures_and_lessons: Branch names are not provenance: experiment/temporal-decay-prototype contains no temporal code at all (only M1/M2 hardware diagnostics); the actual prototype commit deb2d84 lives on main. Verify content, not the label.

The temporal-decay design is blocked on a turbo2 block type that does not exist in this repo; the requant prototype validates vector quality only - never end-task quality and never a real KV cache. No result JSON was committed.
The temporal decay 30-34% memory saving is analytic (run_memory_savings_estimate), not measured on a running cache; treat as ESTIMATE.
The bias-causal explanation (Qwen K-fragility caused by k_proj bias=True) was falsified by the bias-free Qwen3-8B control; section 10 supersedes sections 4/5.3/5.5 of the paper.
The section 3.4 headline turbo3=0.46 anchored the wrong algorithm (Alg 2 QJL vs production Alg 1); corrected to turboMSE3=0.370 in section 10.1. The QJL flavor overstates production by ~0.10 TV.
The probe's central claim - TV predicts downstream quality ('ghost PPL') - has no committed measurement; tv_vs_ppl.py exists but no output JSON and no correlation number in the paper.
T7 (14-config matrix), T8 (layer-0 outlier robustness), T9 (calibration-text dependence) remain unrun; only T5/T6 were closed by the section 10 addendum.
The inner-product error of the 3->2 requant (1.76x worse) was measured in the prototype but never connected to TV or needle-NLL, so its end-task meaning is unknown.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Progressive KV requantization (turbo3->2-bit for old tokens) keeps end-task quality inside the direct-2-bit envelope, so a tiny model can serve longer context in the same RAM.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: On a real model, needle-NLL or PPL under decay-3->2 is worse than direct 2-bit by more than the decay's own cosine gap, or falls off the direct-2-bit baseline.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Run the numpy-only synthetic path of benchmarks/temporal_decay_prototype.py, then a small HF model (e.g. Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B) forward on CPU with a decayed-K hook; no GPU.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: CPU-only; minutes for synthetic, tens of minutes for a 0.5-1.5B CPU forward.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Routing-side TV measured on a few heads is a cheap pre-screen for KV precision: it ranks configs in the same order as downstream needle-NLL/PPL.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: TV vs needle-NLL across configs has Spearman <= 0, or TV ranks the best config worst.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Run villines-probe/tv_vs_ppl.py on a tiny model on CPU, seq 512-1024, configs fp16/turbo5/turbo3/turboMSE3/biassub; correlate TV with needle-NLL.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Per-channel K mean subtraction is a general low-bit-K rescue, and offset_ratio identifies which (layer,head) need it, so a mixed-precision tiny model can keep only the few off-center heads at high precision.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: offset_ratio does not predict TV recovery on a new architecture (Spearman <= 0.5).
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: k_channel_stats.py + tq_collapse_probe.py --bias-corr on a small Qwen and a clean control, all on CPU.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The fixed Walsh-Hadamard rotation already captures the available headroom: TorQuant post-centering first-order saving is <0.6 bits and no head clears 1 bit, so learned rotations are not worth GPU budget for tiny models.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: A learned butterfly rotor beats the fixed WHT by >=1 bit, or by >=0.1 TV at matched bits, on a real model.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Run torquant_certificate.py on a CPU small model, raw vs centered, and compare against a learned-rotor rotation fit on the same K.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: Certificate is CPU-only minutes; the learned-rotor falsifier needs GPU (bank, not now).

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Temporal decay's memory saving is largest exactly where the 8 GB box needs it (long context), so a 2070S serving Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M at 32-48K could fit a larger KV budget by decaying old tokens.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: At 32K on the 2070S, decayed-K PPL exceeds the q8_0-K budget's acceptable delta, or the requant kernel cost exceeds the memory win.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Recompute the analytic KV-size table from run_memory_savings_estimate with the box's real layer/KV-head config and context; no runtime.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: CPU-only, seconds (arithmetic); the falsifier needs the GPU box.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Qwen3.5 (bias-free, QK-norm) will show the same per-channel K off-centering as Qwen3-8B, so the offset screen - not the bias term - should drive K-precision choices for the tiny-model fleet.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Qwen3.5 offset_ratio stays below ~2.5 (Mistral-like) yet still collapses at turboMSE3, or is high yet does not collapse.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Capture Qwen3.5 K on CPU with k_channel_stats.py and run the turboMSE3 sweep; compare offset_ratio max and TV to the Qwen3-8B numbers.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: CPU-only for a small Qwen3.5 variant, under 1h; no GPU.

open_questions: Was the temporal-decay 3->2 prototype ever run end-to-end on a real cache? No output JSON exists; only the commit message.
Does routing-side TV actually predict downstream needle-NLL/PPL? tv_vs_ppl.py exists but no output JSON is committed and the paper reports no correlation.
Why does Qwen3-8B retain a post-centering residual TV of 0.148 vs Mistral's 0.091? Per-channel kurtosis does not predict it (Spearman 0.02).
What exactly is the missing turbo2 block layout/quantizer (2-bit indices + no hi1 bit)? It is not present in this repo.
Does the 3->2 requant preserve inner-product ranking for attention, or only cosine? The 1.76x inner-product error was measured but never linked to TV or needle-NLL.
Where do Qwen3's per-channel K offsets come from if not a bias term - the learned k_proj weights alone? Section 10.3 says yes but does not isolate the channel.
Do T7 (14-config matrix), T8 (layer-0 outlier robustness) and T9 (calibration-text dependence) change any of the section 10 conclusions?
